Key Features: I am calculating deltas between the old and new orders: delta_days: Difference in delivery date (e.g., +5 days delay). delta_qty_pct: Percentage change in quantity (e.g., +0.10 for a 10% increase). Nature of Data: The data is heavily skewed (fat-tailed). Most updates are small (0-5 days), but legitimate business events can cause massive shifts (e.g., 60-day delays) that are not data errors. 3. The Issue: When I applied the standard IQR Method (1.5 * IQR) globally, it removed ~50% of my dataset (dropping from 21k to 10k rows). Why: Because the interquartile range is very tight (most updates are 0), the IQR bounds became extremely narrow (e.g., -14 to +10 days).
